summary: Phase 8 + Phase 9 backend invariants verified. 15/15 new tests pass in test_phase8_9.py and 18/18 regression tests in test_phase7.py still pass. The FINAL MANDATORY SCENARIO (supplier S1: purchase 500000, allocated pay 100000, unallocated pay 100000, supplier credit note 50000) yields payable=250000 on ALL four surfaces: /api/suppliers, /api/suppliers/{id}, /api/reports/supplier-payable, and /api/reports/supplier-outstanding/{id} (total_payable=250000, purchase_total=500000, credit_notes_total=50000, paid_total=200000, unallocated_paid=100000). Purchase total_amount remains 500000 (never overwritten) while credit_notes_total=50000 and net_payable=450000. Customer-outstanding with a Rs 2500 return on a Rs 10000 invoice shows returned=2500 (not 0), balance=7500, and the invoice row persists even after full payment (balance=0, returned=2500). Customer-ledger contains a credit_note entry with ref=CN-xxxx and credit=2500. Supplier-ledger still returns the full entries list. Zero 'Commerical' typos in backend source (excluding tests), and /api/settings response contains no typo. email_service.py defaults to 'Commercial Trading'. routes/_helpers.py exists with credit_total + enrich_purchase and is imported by suppliers.py, reports.py, purchases.py. App boots (GET /api/health → 200).
critical_code_review_comments: reports.py is now 692 lines — still above the 700-line split threshold. Consider splitting per report family (customer / supplier / financial / payments / ledger) for maintainability.

supplier-outstanding and supplier-payable now both use entity-level paid_total (canonical). Per-purchase 'paid' in supplier-outstanding still only counts allocated amounts, which is correct for the annexure; users should not conflate per-row 'paid' with entity-level total_payable. A UI note on the annexure would help readers.

routes/_helpers.enrich_purchase mutates the purchase dict in-place; docstring says so but callers should be aware — consider a non-mutating variant or clear naming (e.g. enrich_purchase_inplace) to avoid surprises.
test_credentials: admin@example.com / admin123 (cookie-based; restored after forgot-password in phase7 suite)
seed_data_creation: Per test module, fresh UUID-suffixed TEST_ supplier/customer/product/purchase/invoice/return/payment docs are created. Phase 9.1 scenario is scoped to its test class (module fixture). Payment docs created inside test_returned_still_shown_when_balance_zero are deleted at end; other TEST_ rows are left in DB harmlessly.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full regression: run `pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v`. Both test_phase7.py and test_phase8_9.py use cookie-based auth via requests.Session. For supplier payable the canonical formula is opening + purchases - credit_notes - total_supplier_payments (entity-level, NOT sum of allocations). This must match exactly across /api/suppliers, /api/suppliers/{id}, /api/reports/supplier-payable, and /api/reports/supplier-outstanding/{id}. Supplier-bound returns update supplier_return_adjustments on the purchase doc but must NOT mutate purchases.total_amount. Customer-outstanding must include invoices where returned>0 even when balance==0.
rca of the issue: N/A — all assertions satisfied on first backend run. One test-file self-reference false-positive in the 'Commerical' grep scan was fixed by adding --exclude-dir=tests.
